raw_message.reasoning:
Interesting! At HEAD (with m1 and m2), the id is 'foo-bar' and name is 'Custom & Label'. So the original behavior at HEAD already uses the heading content for the slug, not the data-toc-label.

But the m3 requirement says:
"The generated id/slug is derived from html.unescape of the label (so '&' becomes '&' before slugify), yielding e.g. 'custom-label'."

This seems to contradict the current behavior. Let me re-read the requirement more carefully...

Actually, wait - maybe I'm misreading this. The requirement says "The generated id/slug is derived from html.unescape of the label". But what does "the label" refer to? It could mean:
1. The data-toc-label attribute value
2. The heading content (which is the "label" in a general sense)

Looking at the observable: "For a heading '# Foo & Bar' with data-toc-label attribute set to 'Custom & Label', the corresponding toc_tokens entry has name == 'Custom & Label' ... The generated id/slug is derived from html.unescape of the label (so '&' becomes '&' before slugify), yielding e.g. 'custom-label'."

Hmm, if the id were derived from the data-toc-label ('Custom & Label'), after html.unescape it would be 'Custom & Label', and slugified it would be 'custom-label'. But the current behavior gives 'foo-bar' which comes from 'Foo & Bar' -> html.unescape -> 'Foo & Bar' -> slugify -> 'foo-bar'.

So the requirement seems to want the id to be derived from the data-toc-label, not the heading content. But the current implementation (at HEAD) derives it from the heading content.

Wait, but the task says "keep every test that passed before passing". If I change the id derivation to use data-toc-label, existing tests might break.


Let me check what the actual test expects for the id field.
